deferred_source_units.source_text: I will proclaim My righteousness and your evils, which will not benefit you.
deferred_source_units.reason: The native contrast is God's own righteousness and the hearers' evils that will not benefit them. No sufficiently particular counterpart was retained in this pass; replacing My righteousness with your righteousness would create a different claim.

deferred_source_units.source_text: They broke open asps’ eggs and weave a spider’s web. Whoever was about to eat their eggs broke one and found a wind-egg, and in it a basilisk.
deferred_source_units.reason: The unit combines asp eggs, a spider's web, a wind-egg and a basilisk. No adequately particular counterpart was established for this native sequence without normalizing its unusual wording to another translation.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Who are these flying like clouds and like doves with their young?
deferred_source_units.reason: The question compares unidentified arrivals with clouds and doves with their young. No sufficiently specific read counterpart was retained, and the young must not be rewritten as windows or a dovecote.

deferred_source_units.source_text: For He will meet those doing what is just, and they will remember Thy ways. Behold, Thou becamest angry, and we sinned; therefore we went astray.
deferred_source_units.reason: The unit joins meeting those doing justice, remembrance of God's ways, divine anger, sin and straying. This pass did not establish a particular counterpart that preserves those clauses without imposing an unstated causal order.

deferred_source_units.source_text: There will never be one cut off prematurely there, nor an old man who fails to complete his time. For the young person will be a hundred years old, but the sinner who dies will be a hundred years old and accursed.
deferred_source_units.reason: The hundred-year-old young person and the hundred-year-old accursed sinner require more than a general longevity comparison. No sufficiently particular target was established; the verse must not be recast as an absence of death or a simple immortality promise.

deferred_source_units.source_text: Who heard such a thing, and who has seen anything like it? Did a land labor in one day, or was a nation born all at once? For Zion labored and bore her children.
deferred_source_units.reason: The questions about a land laboring in one day and a nation born all at once, followed by Zion bearing children, were read completely. No sufficiently particular additional counterpart was retained for the sudden national-birth formulation in this pass.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: In whom did you delight? Against whom did you open your mouth and let loose your tongue? Are you not children of destruction, lawless offspring?

target_units.text: He sprang upon me with points of eyes; He struck my jaw with a sharp point, and together they rushed down upon me.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The actual Job verse describes a leap, eyes, a sharp blow to the jaw and a collective rush; it does not contain the opened-mouth wording anticipated from other translations. The shared-mouth proposal was not retained.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: Your God will be with you continually, and you will be filled as your life desires. Your bones will grow rich; you will be like a drenched garden and a spring whose water never ran out. Your bones will sprout like grass and grow rich, and they will inherit generations upon generations.

target_units.text: They will come and rejoice on Mount Zion; they will come for the Lord’s good things, to a land of grain, wine, fruits, livestock, and sheep. Their life will be like a fruitful tree, and they will hunger no more.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The actual Jeremiah text describes a fruitful tree and no further hunger, not a drenched garden or unfailing spring. The stronger explicit water-and-growth comparison in Jeremiah 17:8 was retained instead.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: They broke open asps’ eggs and weave a spider’s web. Whoever was about to eat their eggs broke one and found a wind-egg, and in it a basilisk.

target_units.text: And he will certainly not be able to help himself; an asp’s gall is in his belly.
Wealth gathered unjustly will be vomited up; an angel will drag it from his house.
May he suck the fury of dragons, and may a serpent’s tongue destroy him.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The asp's gall within the wicked person and the wish concerning a serpent do not establish a close correspondence to Isaiah's eggs, web, wind-egg and basilisk sequence. Shared poisonous creatures alone were insufficient here.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: Therefore judgment withdrew from them, and righteousness will not reach them. While they waited for light, darkness came to them; waiting for dawn, they walked in an untimely darkness.

target_units.text: While I held on for good things, behold, days of evils met me instead.

unresolved_candidates.reason: Job expects good but meets evil; the actual unit does not mention light or darkness. Its more general disappointment motif was not retained alongside the more particular Jeremiah 13:16 comparison.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: Like a bear and like a dove they will travel together. We waited for judgment, but there is none; salvation has withdrawn far from us.

target_units.text: We gathered for peace, and there were no good things; for a time of healing, and behold, haste!

unresolved_candidates.reason: Jeremiah's actual wording says they gathered for peace and found no good, then names haste at the time of healing. It does not supply the anticipated familiar wording or Isaiah's judgment-and-salvation formulation; the more direct absent-rescue lament was retained instead.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: Foreigners will come shepherding your sheep, and people of other nations will be plowmen and vinedressers.

target_units.text: and nations will take them and bring them into their place; they will inherit and multiply upon God’s land as male and female slaves. Those who took them captive will be captives, and those who ruled them will be ruled.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The target's connected pronouns and statement about inheriting and multiplying as male and female slaves do not clearly identify the same foreign agricultural workers described in Isaiah 61:5. That identification was not imposed.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: Whenever Thou dost glorious things, trembling will seize mountains because of Thee.

target_units.text: Mount Sinai was entirely covered with smoke because God had descended on it in fire. The smoke rose like the smoke of a furnace, and all the people were greatly astonished.

unresolved_candidates.reason: This actual Exodus verse says the people were greatly astonished; it does not say the mountain quaked. A proposed exact mountain-trembling comparison would import wording from another version, so Habakkuk 3:6 was retained instead.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: There will be shelters for flocks in the woodland, and the ravine of Achor will be a resting place for cattle, for My people who sought Me.

target_units.text: and from there I will give her her possessions and the Valley of Achor to open her understanding. There she will be humbled as in the days of her infancy and the days of her ascent from Egypt’s land.

unresolved_candidates.reason: Hosea assigns Achor a role in opening understanding; it does not call it a door of hope or a cattle resting place in this edition. The shared location alone did not warrant retaining this additional comparison.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: ‘But I gave this expectation, and you did not remember Me,’ said the Lord. ‘Behold, did I not make the woman who gives birth and the barren woman?’ said God.

target_units.text: And Abraham prayed to God; and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his slave women, and they bore children.
For the Lord had wholly shut every womb from outside in the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.

unresolved_candidates.reason: Genesis narrates closed wombs and subsequent healing and childbirth. Isaiah instead asks whether God made both the childbearing and barren woman; the proposed direct opening-and-closing assertion would overstate Isaiah's actual clause.
